lesson.title: Review Day: Our First Eleven Letters
lesson.subject: punjabi

contentBlocks.text: This week you learned eleven Gurmukhi letters! Today is review day — no new letters, just practice remembering everything you've learned so far.

Say all eleven letters together, in order: ੳ, ਅ, ੲ, ਸ, ਹ, ਕ, ਖ, ਗ, ਘ, ਙ, ਚ. Try covering up the letters one at a time and saying the name from memory. Which letters do you remember easily? Which ones need more practice? That's completely normal — review days are for finding out what to practice more, not for getting everything perfect.
Great work this week! You've built a real foundation for reading Gurmukhi. Next week, we'll keep adding new letters to this list.

objectives: Recall and name all eleven letters learned this week (ੳ, ਅ, ੲ, ਸ, ਹ, ਕ, ਖ, ਗ, ਘ, ਙ, ਚ)
Self-identify which letters are secure and which need more practice, building early metacognitive habits
materialsNeeded: This week's four worksheets, if kept, for a quick flip-back review
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Say all eleven letters together as a group, in order, without looking at any reference.
2. Play a quick game: cover the letters one at a time and ask the child to name each from memory.
3. Notice together which letters were easy and which were tricky — this is useful information, not a test to pass or fail.
4. Move to the worksheet: trace all eleven letters once more, in order.
5. Praise effort and progress, not just correctness — a full week of new letters is real work for a Kindergartner.
6. Close by previewing that next week continues with new letters.
differentiationTips: Struggling: it's completely fine to spend extra review days on this same set of eleven letters before moving on — there's no rush
Ready for more: ask the child to sort the eleven letters into their groups (3 vowel bearers, sassa/haha pair, the ka-row) from memory
For a child who wants a game, turn this into a simple matching or flashcard activity instead of straight tracing
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a review/recall activity — there is no single right/wrong answer. Note which of the eleven letters the child recalled confidently vs. needed prompting for, to guide next week's pacing.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: A dedicated review day after introducing 11 new letters in one week matches how real Gurmukhi primers pace instruction — consolidation before adding more content is essential at this age and this is the first of many planned review days in this course.
